- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F1 contract: QEMU plugin exits with code 200 on drain (matches vsim's
3	# kExitHandoffToQemu). 0 is reserved for "workload completed normally".
4	# The orchestrator (F2+) uses this distinction to decide the next spawn.
5	#
6	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
9	#   VSIM_ELF     a CSR-trigger fixture (default: handoff_roundtrip.elf)
10	
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
15	
16	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
17	hybrid_resolve_paths
18	
19	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
20	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-drain-shared.XXXXXX)
21	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
22	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
23	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
24	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
25	
26	set +e
27	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
28	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
29	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
30	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
31	  -nographic \
32	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
33	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
34	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
35	RC=$?
36	set -e
37	
38	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
39	  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
40	  echo "--- qemu log ---"
41	  cat "$QEMU_LOG"
42	  exit 1
43	fi
44	
45	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
46	  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: state file is empty"
47	  exit 1
48	fi
49	
50	echo "[plugin_drain_exit_code] PASS: QEMU exit=$RC, state size=$(wc -c <"$STATE_QEMU") bytes"
51

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# v5 contract: the QEMU plugin drains the L2C MMIO register window into
3	# hybrid_state_v1. The l2c_drain fixture writes 0xA5 to the L2C Control Register
4	# (0xE0500008) and then hits the ROI entry marker; the plugin must set
5	# HYBRID_FLAG_L2C and capture 0xA5 at hybrid_l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL/8].
6	#
7	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
8	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
9	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
10	#   VSIM_ELF     the l2c_drain fixture (FIXTURE=l2c_drain)
11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
16	
17	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-l2c_drain}"
18	hybrid_resolve_paths
19	
20	REPO_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
22	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-l2c-shared.XXXXXX)
23	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
24	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
25	CHECK_SRC=$(mktemp --suffix=.c)
26	CHECK_BIN=$(mktemp)
27	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG" "$CHECK_SRC" "$CHECK_BIN"' EXIT
28	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
29	
30	set +e
31	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
32	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
33	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
34	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
35	  -nographic \
36	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
37	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
38	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
39	RC=$?
40	set -e
41	
42	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
43	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
44	  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
45	  exit 1
46	fi
47	
48	# Inspect the drained struct via a tiny C checker that shares the ABI header,
49	# so the field offset stays robust to layout changes.
50	cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
51	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
52	#include <stdio.h>
53	#include <stdlib.h>
54	int main(int argc, char **argv) {
55	    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
56	    if (!f) { fprintf(stderr, "open %s failed\n", argv[1]); return 2; }
57	    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
58	    size_t n = fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f);
59	    fclose(f);
60	    if (n != sizeof(s)) { fprintf(stderr, "short read %zu != %zu\n", n, sizeof(s)); return 3; }
61	    if (s.magic != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC) { fprintf(stderr, "bad magic\n"); return 4; }
62	    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
63	    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
64	    unsigned long long want = strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 0);
65	    if (ctrl != want) { fprintf(stderr, "l2c ctrl=0x%llx want=0x%llx\n", ctrl, want); return 6; }
66	    printf("OK: HYBRID_FLAG_L2C set, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
67	    return 0;
68	}
69	EOF
70	cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"
71	
72	if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU" 0xA5; then
73	  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_drain]"
74	else
75	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: L2C register window not drained correctly"
76	  exit 1
77	fi
78

34	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \

41	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"

45	cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
46	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"

49	    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
50	    if (!f) return 2;
51	    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
52	    if (fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f) != sizeof(s)) return 3;
53	    fclose(f);
54	    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
55	    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
56	    if ((ctrl & 0x1u) != 0x1u) { fprintf(stderr, "CEN not set: l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl); return 6; }
57	    printf("OK: reset default CEN=1, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
58	    return 0;
59	}
60	EOF
61	cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"
62	
63	if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU"; then
64	  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_reset_default]"
65	else
66	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: L2C reset default CEN=1 not observed"
67	  exit 1
68	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# v6 contract: the QEMU plugin tracks which mask-governed CSRs the guest WROTE
3	# and drains that as write_mask[] under HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK. The wm_drain
4	# fixture writes mxstatus + mcache_ctl (read-modify-write-same), and only READS
5	# mmisc_ctl, so:
6	#   - HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK set
7	#   - mxstatus + mcache_ctl bits SET
8	#   - mmisc_ctl bit CLEAR (a csrr must not count as a write)
9	#   - ucode bit SET unconditionally (DSP ops update it without a CSR insn)
10	#
11	# Required environment (auto-detected):
12	#   VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF (FIXTURE=wm_drain)

61	    int mxstatus = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_ANDES_BASE + HYBRID_WM_ANDES_IDX_mxstatus);
62	    int mcache   = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_MCACHE_CTL);
63	    int mmisc    = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_MMISC_CTL);
64	    int ucode    = hybrid_wm_test(s.write_mask, HYBRID_WM_ANDES_BASE + HYBRID_WM_ANDES_IDX_ucode);
65	    if (!mxstatus) { fprintf(stderr, "mxstatus bit clear (csrw not tracked)\n"); return 6; }
66	    if (!mcache)   { fprintf(stderr, "mcache_ctl bit clear (csrw not tracked)\n"); return 7; }
67	    if (mmisc)     { fprintf(stderr, "mmisc_ctl bit SET (csrr wrongly counted as write)\n"); return 8; }
68	    if (!ucode)    { fprintf(stderr, "ucode bit clear (must be transport-always)\n"); return 9; }
69	    printf("OK: mask=%016llx %016llx (mxstatus+mcache_ctl set, mmisc_ctl clear, ucode always)\n",
70	           (unsigned long long) s.write_mask[1], (unsigned long long) s.write_mask[0]);
71	    return 0;
72	}

74	cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"

76	if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU"; then
77	  echo "PASS[plugin_write_mask]"
78	else
79	  echo "FAIL[plugin_write_mask]: write-mask not drained correctly"
80	  exit 1
81	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# LM transport (F0/F1) + HVM transport (F2) contract: the QEMU plugin drains
3	# ILM/DLM/HVM CONTENT into raw sidecar files next to the state outfile. The
4	# lm_drain fixture writes known patterns into the hart-0 LM slave ports (ILM
5	# 0xA0000000, DLM 0xA0200000) and the HVM aperture (0x90000000) at the first
6	# and last word of each drained span; the plugin, given the *_size= args,
7	# must write <outfile>.ilm (65536 B), .dlm (32768 B) and .hvm (262144 B)
8	# carrying those patterns. A run WITHOUT the size args (the no-LM/HVM-engine
9	# default) must produce NO sidecar files. QEMU's default HVM is 1 byte
10	# (hvm_size_pow_2=0), so both runs sync the geometry via -global -- the raw
11	# analog of the driver's -readconfig path, which already carries it.
12	#
13	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
14	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
15	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
16	#   VSIM_ELF     the lm_drain fixture (FIXTURE=lm_drain)
17	
18	set -euo pipefail
19	
20	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
21	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
22	
23	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_drain}"
24	hybrid_resolve_paths
25	
26	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
27	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-lm-shared.XXXXXX)
28	STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
29	STATE_QEMU="$STATE_DIR/state.bin"
30	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
31	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$QEMU_LOG"; rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"' EXIT
32	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
33	
34	run_qemu() {  # $1 = extra plugin args appended after outfile ("" for none)
35	  set +e
36	  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
37	    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
38	    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
39	    -global driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=hvm_size_pow_2,value=18 \
40	    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
41	    -nographic \
42	    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
43	    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
44	    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU$1" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
45	  RC=$?
46	  set -e
47	}
48	
49	check_word() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 expected LE word (8 hex digits)
50	  local got
51	  got=$(od -An -tx4 -j "$2" -N4 "$1" | tr -d ' \n')
52	  if [ "$got" != "$3" ]; then
53	    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: $1 @ offset $2 = '$got', want '$3'"
54	    exit 1
55	  fi
56	}
57	
58	# --- Run 1: sizes given -> sidecars written with the fixture's patterns ---
59	run_qemu ",ilm_size=65536,dlm_size=32768,hvm_size=262144"
60	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
61	  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
62	  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
63	  exit 1
64	fi
65	for spec in "$STATE_QEMU.ilm:65536" "$STATE_QEMU.dlm:32768" \
66	            "$STATE_QEMU.hvm:262144"; do
67	  path="${spec%:*}"; want="${spec#*:}"
68	  if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
69	    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: missing sidecar $path"; exit 1
70	  fi
71	  size=$(stat -c%s "$path")
72	  if [ "$size" -ne "$want" ]; then
73	    echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: $path size=$size want=$want"; exit 1
74	  fi
75	done
76	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.ilm" 0     494c4d30   # "ILM0" at window start
77	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.ilm" 65532 494c4d31   # "ILM1" at last drained word
78	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 0     444c4d30   # "DLM0" at window start
79	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 32764 444c4d31   # "DLM1" at last drained word
80	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.hvm" 0      48564d30  # "HVM0" at window start
81	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.hvm" 262140 48564d31  # "HVM1" at last drained word
82	
83	# --- Run 2: no size args (default 0 = no-LM/HVM engine) -> NO sidecar files ---
84	rm -f "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_QEMU.ilm" "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" "$STATE_QEMU.hvm"
85	run_qemu ""
86	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
87	  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: (no-size run) expected exit=200, got $RC"
88	  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
89	  exit 1
90	fi
91	if [ -e "$STATE_QEMU.ilm" ] || [ -e "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" ] \
92	   || [ -e "$STATE_QEMU.hvm" ]; then
93	  echo "FAIL[plugin_lm_drain]: sidecar files written without *_size args"
94	  exit 1
95	fi
96	
97	echo "PASS[plugin_lm_drain]"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
3	#
4	# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
5	# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
6	# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
7	# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
8	# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
9	# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
10	# insn runs inside the measured window.
11	#
12	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
13	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
14	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
15	#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)
16	
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
21	
22	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
23	hybrid_resolve_paths
24	
25	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
26	command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
27	ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
28	[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
29	ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")
30	
31	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
32	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
33	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
34	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
35	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
36	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
37	
38	set +e
39	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
40	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
41	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
42	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
43	  -nographic \
44	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
45	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
46	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
47	  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
48	RC=$?
49	set -e
50	
51	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
52	  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
53	  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
54	  exit 1
55	fi
56	if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
57	  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
58	  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
59	  exit 1
60	fi
61	echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# B13 lint: the plugin's atomic state writer must use mkstemp (or
3	# mkostemp / g_mkstemp), not a getpid()-based tmp filename.
4	#
5	# Under heavy PID churn (test runner forking 128 QEMUs per minute on a
6	# 128-core host) PID reuse can shadow a still-open tmp from a sibling
7	# leg. mkstemp adds a 6-char random suffix and atomically reserves the
8	# inode, eliminating the race window.
9	
10	set -uo pipefail
11	
12	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
13	SRC="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c"
14	
15	fail() { echo "FAIL[plugin_atomic_write_mkstemp]: $1"; exit 1; }
16	
17	[ -r "$SRC" ] || fail "cannot read $SRC"
18	
19	# The tmp-file mechanics live in write_blob_atomic (shared by the state file
20	# and the LM sidecars); write_state_atomic must route through it. Inspect only
21	# those two function bodies so unrelated getpid() uses elsewhere in the file
22	# are not in scope.
23	blob=$(awk '/^static int write_blob_atomic/,/^}/' "$SRC")
24	[ -n "$blob" ] || fail "write_blob_atomic body not located"
25	
26	if echo "$blob" | grep -q "getpid()"; then
27	  fail "write_blob_atomic still composes tmp filename with getpid(); use mkstemp"
28	fi
29	
30	if ! echo "$blob" | grep -qE "mkstemp|g_mkstemp|mkostemp"; then
31	  fail "write_blob_atomic does not call mkstemp; PID collisions possible"
32	fi
33	
34	state=$(awk '/^static int write_state_atomic/,/^}/' "$SRC")
35	[ -n "$state" ] || fail "write_state_atomic body not located"
36	
37	if ! echo "$state" | grep -qE "write_blob_atomic|mkstemp|g_mkstemp|mkostemp"; then
38	  fail "write_state_atomic bypasses write_blob_atomic; PID collisions possible"
39	fi
40	
41	echo "[plugin_atomic_write_mkstemp] PASS"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
3	# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
4	# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
5	#
6	# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
7	# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
8	# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
9	# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
10	# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
11	#
12	# Cases:
13	#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
14	#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
15	#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
16	#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
17	#   3. drain_pc=0x... -- sample at a later, caller-chosen pc instead of the
18	#                        very next insn. The differential harness passes
19	#                        vsim's actual halt pc here: vsim's DMI halt lands a
20	#                        variable 0-3 insns past the trigger, and both sides
21	#                        must sample the SAME architectural point.
22	#   4. drain_pc=0x... alone -- install error: drain_pc requires an oracle
23	#                        anchor (exit_marker / exit_pc).
24	#
25	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
26	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
27	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
28	#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)
29	
30	set -uo pipefail
31	
32	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
33	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
34	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
35	
36	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
37	hybrid_resolve_paths
38	
39	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
40	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
41	command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }
42	
43	MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
44	  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
45	EXIT_PC="0x${MARKERS##* }"
46	# The exit marker is a 4-byte NOP that falls through, so the first insn
47	# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.
48	WANT_PC=$(printf '0x%x' $((EXIT_PC + 4)))
49	
50	STATE=$(mktemp)
51	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
52	trap 'rm -f "$STATE" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
53	
54	run_qemu() {  # $1 = plugin arg suffix (script runs without -e; RC checked per case)
55	  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
56	    -machine andes_ae350 \
57	    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
58	    -nographic \
59	    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
60	    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
61	    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,$1" \
62	    </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
63	  RC=$?
64	}
65	
66	check_drain() {  # $1 = case label
67	  if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
68	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
69	    tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
70	    exit 1
71	  fi
72	  if [ ! -s "$STATE" ]; then
73	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: no state file written"
74	    exit 1
75	  fi
76	  if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$WANT_PC)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
77	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: drain pc != exit-marker+4 ($WANT_PC):"
78	    grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
79	    exit 1
80	  fi
81	}
82	
83	# Case 1: marker mode.
84	run_qemu "exit_marker=1"
85	check_drain "exit_marker"
86	
87	# Case 2: pc mode, boundary = the exit marker's own vaddr.
88	: > "$STATE"
89	run_qemu "exit_pc=$EXIT_PC"
90	check_drain "exit_pc"
91	
92	# Case 3: drain_pc skips past intermediate ticks and samples the chosen pc.
93	# Use the third insn after the exit marker (straight-line in rt_c_hello's
94	# epilogue), derived from the disassembly so insn sizes don't matter.
95	DRAIN_PC=0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '
96	  /5a102013/ { n = NR }
97	  n && NR == n + 3 { sub(/:$/, "", $1); print $1; exit }')

99	run_qemu "exit_marker=1,drain_pc=$DRAIN_PC"
100	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ] || ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$DRAIN_PC)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
101	  echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: drain_pc: expected drain at $DRAIN_PC (rc=$RC):"
102	  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
103	  exit 1
104	fi
105	
106	# Case 4: drain_pc needs an oracle anchor (exit_marker / exit_pc).
107	run_qemu "drain_pc=$DRAIN_PC"
108	if [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || ! grep -qi "drain_pc.*requires" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
109	  echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: bare drain_pc should fail install (got rc=$RC):"
110	  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
111	  exit 1
112	fi
113	
114	echo "[oracle_exit_drain] PASS: oracle drains after the ROI exit boundary (pc=$WANT_PC)"

2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
23	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
24	#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides
25	#                              it) matches this grep -E pattern -- the hook
26	#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
27	#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
28	#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
29	#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
30	#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
31	#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
32	#                        (negative-control knob).
33	#   CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1  assert the vsim leg dumped its exit-time LM
34	#                        content next to its state file AND that it equals
35	#                        the entry-time content byte-for-byte (valid for a
36	#                        ROI that does not WRITE the TCM -- closes the
37	#                        transport loop through the real RTL SRAM).
38	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
39	#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
40	#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
41	#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a

96	# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
97	# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
98	# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
99	# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
100	# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
101	VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
102	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")

105	V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
106	SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
107	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
